summary: I OWN src/train/api.py AND CHANGED ONLY DOCSTRINGS IN IT -- proved, not asserted: an AST comparison of HEAD:src/train/api.py against the working copy with every docstring replaced by a placeholder is IDENTICAL, so not one executable statement moved. That is the right shape for two NARROWER_THAN_CLAIMED verdicts: the mechanism was correct and the SENTENCES around it overreached. BOTH OF MINE RE-VERIFIED AT HEAD BEFORE I TOUCHED ANYTHING, both reproduce digit-for-digit, and both are now fixed. (1) The 'WHAT IT DOES NOT BUY' paragraph said torch DRAW ORDER is 'a channel between packages' and D12 said it 'still moves the numbers of every package downstream of it'. I re-measured both halves. BUILD-TIME IS INERT: injecting 1 or 3 extra global draws right after src/lm/api.py::build_model leaves all 363 built values byte-identical (34acff0aeb14dd4b in all three) while LM.encode moves 26905f117c4d32e7 -> 773820fb538ba090 -> 0b850362297af161; and LM_LAYERS 2 vs 4 moves NO value outside LM -- the only non-LM keys that differ are geometry.layers, geometry.param_estimate and the manifest row for lm.layers, i.e. the lever's own declared value, not drift. RUNTIME IS SINGLE-ENDED: all twelve explicit RNG-consuming torch calls in src/ pass generator= a named stream, TOK's dropout draws from stream.random() and not torch at all, and nn.Dropout / nn.TransformerEncoderLayer / nn.GRU are constructed ONLY in src/lm/api.py -- so LM is the only package drawing from the global at runtime, which is why the exhibition needs a probe on the far side. The docstring now carries both measurements, the LM_DROPOUT=0.0 control, and the two conditions that ARM the wide claim. (2) Process.torch_seed's 'is what makes seeding a DECLARED setting' is true only once something says it out loud; nothing does. The grep returns hits only inside my file plus one prose line in .rework/DECISIONS.md, and the same grep for tf32_applied and amp_state outside my file returns NOTHING -- so it is the P5 layer missing uniformly, and I said exactly what would turn it into a defect. The record is a SNAPSHOT and goes stale silently (torch.manual_seed(999) afterwards -> field 3734753547471956429 vs torch.initial_seed() 999, nothing notices); that is correct semantics and the docstring now says so instead of overclaiming. I also repaired a third, smaller overreach my own edit created: the LEVERS READ line said 'the three paragraphs above' and my narrowing grew one of the three into five -- a paragraph COUNT is the prose form of the stale line number O12 refuses, so it now names the section. FINDINGS 3 AND 4 ARE REAL AT HEAD AND ARE NOT MINE TO FIX: both re-verified by running them, both live entirely in files I do not own, and I edited none of them. Full suite green after all work; RUN's K4 harvest still credits seed.

findings.detail: CONFIRMED AT HEAD AND FIXED. The claim, not the mechanism, was wrong. THE LIMITATION IS REAL: I reran the exhibition and got the verifier's numbers exactly -- LM_ARCH=transformer LM_DROPOUT=0.2, LM_LAYERS 2 vs 4, downstream nn.Linear(4,4) 5f87be0f2321e508 vs 36dc18c1f2e82308 and the following torch.rand(3) [0.18013722,0.73333818,0.01200253] vs [0.62094098,0.40641177,0.740619], with the LM_DROPOUT=0.0 CONTROL making both depths identical (31a48739b3d15e14, [0.41499043,0.43999398,0.09452492]). THE OVERREACH IS THE SCOPE. src/train/api.py::process_setup said torch DRAW ORDER 'remains a channel between packages that no wire declares', and .rework/DECISIONS.md D12 said it 'still moves the numbers of every package downstream of it'. I checked both halves by running them. BUILD-TIME HALF INERT: with PERTURB_DRAWS injecting 1 or 3 extra global torch.rand draws immediately after src/lm/api.py::build_model returns, all 363 values a compose() builds are byte-identical (digest 34acff0aeb14dd4b at n=0, 1 and 3) while LM.encode moves every time (26905f117c4d32e7 -> 773820fb538ba090 -> 0b850362297af161). REAL-LEVER FORM AGREES: LM_LAYERS 2 vs 4 gives 27 differing keys of which the only non-LM three are geometry.layers (2 vs 4), geometry.param_estimate (1458176 vs 1851392) and manifest['lm.layers'] -- the lever's OWN DECLARED value, not RNG drift; no tensor outside LM moves. CAUSE, structural: every package that constructs an nn.Module overwrites every parameter from its own named stream (src/lm/api.py::build_model's named_parameters loop, src/sig/api.py::_Encoder, src/fabric/api.py::build's pop.modules loop, src/world/api.py::build). RUNTIME HALF SINGLE-ENDED: a broadened grep (I widened the verifier's pattern to include in-place samplers) finds TWELVE explicit RNG-consuming torch calls in src/ -- src/fabric/api.py 266,267,293; src/sig/api.py 59,60,189,574,575,658; src/world/api.py 147,158; src/lm/api.py 407 -- and EVERY ONE passes generator=. TOK's segmentation dropout uses `stream.random()` in src/tok/api.py::_segment, not torch. nn.Dropout, nn.TransformerEncoderLayer, nn.TransformerEncoder and nn.GRU are constructed ONLY in src/lm/api.py. So LM is the only package that draws from the global at runtime. THE FIX: the paragraph now keeps the limitation and adds the measured scope -- the build-time result with its digests, the real-lever result naming the three declarative keys, the runtime inventory, the exhibition WITH its control, and the honest closing sentence that the channel is real and live with EXACTLY ONE DRAWER and arms the moment a SECOND package draws from the global at runtime or any package is constructed lazily after a forward. NOT FIXED, NOT MINE: .rework/DECISIONS.md line 263 still carries the wide sentence verbatim; my docstring now quotes it and marks it as wider than the tree, so a reader arriving from either side lands on the correction.

findings.detail: CONFIRMED AT HEAD AND FIXED. Both greps reproduce exactly. `grep -rn torch_seed src/ tests/ docs/ tools/` returns hits ONLY in src/train/api.py (plus its own .pyc), and one prose line at .rework/DECISIONS.md:242 -- no check, no banner, no other package reads Process.torch_seed. `grep -rnE 'tf32_applied|amp_state' src/ tests/ docs/ tools/` outside src/train/api.py returns NOTHING, so the two siblings on the same record stand in exactly the same place: this is the P5 reporting layer not existing yet, uniformly, not a hole peculiar to the seed. THE STALENESS REPRODUCES: process_setup() then torch.manual_seed(999) leaves Process.torch_seed == 3734753547471956429 while torch.initial_seed() == 999, and nothing notices -- no gate, no warning, no exception. THE OVERREACHING SENTENCE was the Process docstring's 'It is what makes seeding that generator a DECLARED setting rather than a silent global side effect'. A field is a place to PUT a declaration; the declaration happens when something says it out loud. THE FIX, three parts, all in src/train/api.py: (a) the record's own sentence is narrowed from 'IS ACTUALLY RUNNING ON' to 'WAS RUNNING ON WHEN THIS RECORD WAS MADE'; (b) a new paragraph states the measurement -- DECLARABLE not yet DECLARED, both greps quoted, the siblings named as what keeps it a narrowing rather than a hole, and the exact condition that turns it into a real defect (a P5 banner printing tf32_applied and amp_state and leaving torch_seed out); (c) a second new paragraph states the snapshot semantics with the torch.manual_seed(999) result, why a live-reading property would be WORSE (it would always agree with reality but attribute a later write to this function), and therefore why the comparison is an act a reader performs rather than a property the field keeps. process_setup's DID IT FIRE line is narrowed to match: 'what torch WAS running on when this function returned', plus 'ALL THREE ARE DECLARED AND, AT HEAD, UNREAD'. The read-back itself is untouched and still genuine.
